title: Python attribute-write binder side: dotted class targets, module-global class rebinding, type(self) and __class__ writes, aliases and del (DEC-303 a79/a80 GCLI-151a)
description: Record-only held task, the binder-side half (leader label GCLI-151a) of GCLI-151 split under DEC-303 (a80) item 6 (opum-ai/opum-doc#2083, ODOC-640). Scope is the write-recording half of the (a79) Q-C and (a80) item 3 shapes: a write that is not recorded, or is recorded on the wrong target. Shapes and their dev results, measured 2026-11-27 at origin/dev 1ea3432: (2) dotted class targets Outer.Inner.m = v and m.D.m = v through an import, not recorded, wrong edges Outer.Inner.m and m.py:D.m; (3) a module-global class rebound m.C = other, not recorded because the chain resolves to a class symbol, and the linchpin the read half consumes; (4) type(self).m = v and self.__class__.m = v, recorded as nothing, wrong edge C.m; (11) N1 aliases K = C; K.m = other, import m; n = m; n.f = other, k = cls; k.m = other and k = type(self); k.m = other, none recorded on the target; (15) N5 del C.m and del self.m must count as writes, as GCLI-115 counts del for names, not counted, wrong edge C.m. Build in the order #3, then #2, #4, #11, #15. Be sure #3 alone changes only refusals; test every reader of the recorded write, including the base position and the two-argument super() first argument that (a80) deliberately keeps write-blind, because a binder change can make a resolution fall back to another edge (the round-2 lesson). Any created in-repo edge comes to opum-doc via the leader before the PR.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each binder shape is recorded against its target with a red-before green-after fixture and a resolving twin: #2 dotted class targets, #3 module-global class rebound m.C = other, #4 type(self).m and self.__class__.m, #11 N1 class, module and receiver aliases, #15 del C.m and del self.m
A mutant per recorded path is observed red on its predicted fixture

Removal-only holds: the subset check with flags over the five pins, every fixture and the 1394-source corpus shows no created in-repo edge, with an observed-red control; every removed edge is named in the PR
No DEC-182 path class is touched and no dependency is added

plan: Claim the task, branch off origin/dev, read DEC-303 (a79)/(a80) and this record before code.

#3 first: record m.C = other (a module-global class rebound through its module) as a module attribute write on m; confirm #3 alone changes only refusals and that no reader (including base position and two-argument super first argument, write-blind per (a80)) creates an edge.
#2: resolve a dotted class target to its class symbol and record the class attribute write on it.
#4: classify type(self).m and self.__class__.m as class-level writes on the receiver class.
#11: follow single-binding aliases (K = C, n = m, k = cls, k = type(self)) to the class, module or receiver before recording.
#15: record del C.m and del self.m as attribute writes, as GCLI-115 counts del for names.

Prove: red-before/green-after fixtures with twins, a mutant per path red, removal-only by the subset check with flags over the five pins, every fixture and the corpus with an observed-red control; report created/removed edges; then the leader clears head-pinned.
implementationNotes: SPLIT under DEC-303 (a80) item 6 from GCLI-151. This is the binder half (leader label GCLI-151a); the read half is the read-side one-path task, the heavy reads the heavy task. All three hold the (a36) item 8 pre-registration and come ahead of GCLI-141 to 143.

SHAPE TABLE, dev measured 2026-11-27 at origin/dev 1ea3432, via analyzePythonCalls with with-write/without-write twins: #2 dotted class target Outer.Inner.m=other same-module and m.D.m=other through import, wrong edges Outer.Inner.m and m.py:D.m; #3 m.C=other not recorded (chain resolves to class symbol), so from-import and base paths resolve; #4 type(self).m=other and self.__class__.m=other, wrong edge C.m; #11 K=C;K.m=other, import m;n=m;n.f=other, k=cls;k.m=other, k=type(self);k.m=other, wrong edges C.m, m.py:f, C.m, C.m; #15 del C.m and del self.m, wrong edge C.m.

(a80) keeps the module-attribute gate write-blind in two positions, a class name in a base position and a two-argument super() first argument, so those paths behave as on dev. #3 must not turn them into created edges; the removal-only subset check with flags is the guard.
Files expected: src/python/calls.ts (recordAttributeWrite and helpers) and test/python-hops.test.ts. No DEC-182 path class; no dependency.

BUILT on branch fix/GCLI-154-attribute-write-binder off dev 2d9ea92. Files src/python/calls.ts and test/python-hops.test.ts: (2) dotted class targets Outer.Inner.m and m.D.m resolve to their class symbol and are recorded as class-level writes; (3) m.C = other was already recorded — pinned, no code; (4) type(self).m (new describeCallee typeArg, plus a tree-sitter type_alias_statement misparse re-dispatch) and self.__class__.m are class-level writes on the receiver; (11) single-binding aliases K=C, n=m, k=cls, k=type(self)/self.__class__ are followed (with a binding-line order guard) to the class or module; (15) del C.m and del self.m are recorded through the same classifier. PROOF: 20 GCLI-154 fixtures, 13 red on dev and all green on the head; 6 mutants (dotted, type(self), __class__, alias, del, gate-restore) each red on a predicted subset, none unexpected; subset check with flags over the five pins (483 files) 0 created 0 removed (identical bins), the 1394-source corpus 0/0, and the fixture sources created 0 with 11 intended removals, the 3-base and 3-super write-blind sources unchanged; comparator control red on an injected created edge. Full suite 1300 pass; typecheck clean; lint one pre-existing warning (calls.ts useConst); format:check clean. No created in-repo edge; no DEC-182 path class; no dependency.

DEC-303 (a82) (opum-ai/opum-doc#2085, ODOC-640): (1) #3 is a pinning fixture with write-blind controls and no code — accepted; (a81) item 1's linchpin premise corrected, order unchanged (GCLI-155 depends on GCLI-154). (2) Plan accepted with one #11 clarification, now built: an alias whose bindings are ALL enumerable records the write on EVERY class or module it may be bound to (K = C; K = D; K.m refuses on both), not only a single-binding alias; an alias with a binding that cannot be enumerated is the named blind spot — it falls through to the local write and goes into GCLI-156's measurement, not built here. UPDATED PROOF after (a82): 21 GCLI-154 fixtures, 16 fail on origin/dev and all 21 pass on the head; 6 mutants each red on a predicted subset (the alias mutant covers single, module, classmethod, type(self), nested, multi-binding and order), none unexpected; subset check with flags: five pins (483 files) 0 created 0 removed, the 1394-source corpus 0/0, fixture sources 0 created with 14 intended removals (multi-binding removes app.py:C.m and app.py:D.m; the blind spot source stays resolving), the 3-base and 3-super write-blind sources unchanged; full suite 1301 pass; typecheck clean; lint one pre-existing warning; format:check clean. No created in-repo edge.

DEC-303 (a83) (opum-ai/opum-doc#2086, ODOC-640), round 1 A: a created edge is not accepted, #236 stays removal-only. Changes on top of a4e104f: (1) F1 fixed — the type_alias misparse branch now KEEPS dev's rebound binding for the climbed target name (marked typeAliasMisparse so the write classification can still resolve type(self)), so self.n()/x.m() refuse exactly as on dev (no created C.n/C.m edge), while the recorded C.m write still refuses OTHER receivers (removal-only). (2) F3 fixed — k = self is an INSTANCE write through an alias (classLevel false), so D's super().m() resolves as on dev; classLevel is true only for a class receiver. (3) F4 fixed — the alias RHS is resolved in found.scope (where the alias is bound), not the write's scope. (4) F5: type-shadow guard added to the type(self) branch. Fixtures: added (a), (b) function, (b) module and F3 with full callees and bins as dev-equal controls; item-2 neighbour/receiver reads for #2, #4, #11, #15; relabelled the #4 nested-def and #15 comprehension as controls. PROOF after a83: 29 GCLI-154 tests, 19 fail on origin/dev and all 29 pass on the head; 7 mutants (M2 dotted, M4 type(self), M4 __class__, M11 alias, M11b multi-binding, M15 del, gate-restore) each red on a predicted subset including the item-2 fixtures, none unexpected; subset check with flags: five pins (483 files) 0 created 0 removed, the 1394-source corpus 0/0, fixture sources 0 created with 21 intended removals and the (a)/(b)/module/F3 controls absent (dev-equal); comparator observed-red control red on an injected created edge. Full suite 1309 pass; typecheck clean; lint one pre-existing warning (useConst); format:check clean. Created edges: 0.
